# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Itohara_2022_everolimus"))$reference`
* Description (final model): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Itohara_2022_everolimus"))$description`
* Description (model with the prior tacrolimus D/C ratio): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Itohara_2022_everolimus_prior_tacrolimus"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.13389>

Itohara and colleagues built the first population PK model of everolimus in
liver transplant recipients from routine therapeutic-drug-monitoring (TDM)
troughs at Kyoto University Hospital. The final model (Table 2) is a
one-compartment model with first-order absorption:

$$\mathrm{CL/F} = 6.89 \times \left(\tfrac{BW}{57}\right)^{0.75}
\times \left(\tfrac{TDD}{1.0}\right)^{0.310} \times 0.823^{FLCZ}
\times \left(\tfrac{eGFR}{55.2}\right)^{0.258} \times 1.23^{Female}\ \mathrm{L/h}$$

$$V_d/F = 312 \times \tfrac{BW}{57}\ \mathrm{L}, \qquad k_a = 6.07\ \mathrm{h^{-1}}\ (\text{fixed})$$

The total-daily-dose term is what the authors call a *TDM effect*: doses were
titrated to a 3-8 ng/mL trough, so patients who cleared everolimus faster were
given more of it. It is not evidence of nonlinear PK, and in a simulation the
covariate column must track the dose actually given.

In a second analysis restricted to the 80 patients who were on tacrolimus before
everolimus was started, the pre-everolimus tacrolimus dose-per-trough (D/C)
ratio was retained as a further covariate on CL/F and all parameters were
re-estimated (Results, equation following Figure 4). That model is packaged as
`Itohara_2022_everolimus_prior_tacrolimus`.

# Population

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Itohara_2022_everolimus"))$population)
```

87 Japanese adult (> 16 years) liver transplant recipients contributed 937
whole-blood everolimus concentrations (Table 1: median age 60 years, range
20-77; body weight 57.0 kg, 34.5-91.0; 46 women; eGFR 55.2 mL/min/1.73 m^2,
11.4-223.7; everolimus total daily dose 1.0 mg/day, 0.25-4.0; 21 patients on
fluconazole). Almost every sample was a trough: no concentration was drawn in
the first 10 h after a dose. Thirteen children (373 concentrations) were used
only for external evaluation.

# Virtual cohort

The cohort resembles the adult Table 1 population, every patient on the
0.5 mg twice-daily regimen the authors recommend (total daily dose 1.0 mg/day).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2022)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_sub, log(57), 0.22), 34.5), 91),
  CRCL = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_sub, log(55.2), 0.5), 11.4), 223.7),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 46 / 87),
  CONMED_FLUCONAZOLE = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 21 / 87),
  DOSE_EVEROLIMUS_MGD = 1.0
)
summary(cohort[, c("WT", "CRCL", "SEXF", "CONMED_FLUCONAZOLE")])
```

# Simulation: concentration-time profile over 14 days

```{r sim-profile}
mod <- readModelDb("Itohara_2022_everolimus")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2022)

dose_times <- seq(0, 13.5 * 24, by = 12)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 14 * 24, by = 2), 13 * 24 + seq(0, 12, by = 0.5))))
events <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::crossing(id = cohort$id, time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 0.5, cmt = "depot"),
  tidyr::crossing(id = cohort$id, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, everything())

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc), n_distinct(sim$id) == n_sub)

sim |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(3, 8), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Everolimus whole-blood concentration (ng/mL)",
    title = "0.5 mg twice daily: median and 90% prediction interval",
    caption = "Dashed lines: the 3-8 ng/mL target trough range."
  )
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 3: steady-state troughs by body weight, eGFR, sex and fluconazole

Figure 3 simulated troughs at 0.5 mg twice daily (5000 replicates per scenario;
200 here), varying body weight (30, 60, 90 kg) at eGFR 55.2, and eGFR (15, 30,
60, 90 mL/min/1.73 m^2) at 57 kg, for each sex with and without fluconazole.

```{r fig3}
scen <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::crossing(panel = "Body weight", WT = c(30, 60, 90), CRCL = 55.2),
  tidyr::crossing(panel = "eGFR", WT = 57, CRCL = c(15, 30, 60, 90))
) |>
  tidyr::crossing(SEXF = c(0L, 1L), CONMED_FLUCONAZOLE = c(0L, 1L)) |>
  mutate(scenario = row_number())

n_rep <- 200
fig3_events <- bind_rows(
  scen |> mutate(evid = 1L, time = 0, amt = 0.5, cmt = "depot", ii = 12, ss = 1L),
  scen |> mutate(evid = 0L, time = 12, amt = 0, cmt = "central", ii = 0, ss = 0L)
) |>
  tidyr::crossing(rep = seq_len(n_rep)) |>
  mutate(id = (scenario - 1L) * n_rep + rep, DOSE_EVEROLIMUS_MGD = 1.0) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, ii, ss, everything())

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2023)
fig3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, fig3_events,
  keep = c("panel", "scenario"), maxsteps = 500000L, returnType = "data.frame"
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(fig3$Cc), n_distinct(fig3$id) == nrow(scen) * n_rep)

fig3 <- fig3 |>
  mutate(
    sex = ifelse(SEXF == 1, "Female", "Male"),
    flcz = ifelse(CONMED_FLUCONAZOLE == 1, "FLCZ +", "FLCZ -"),
    level = ifelse(panel == "Body weight", paste(WT, "kg"), paste("eGFR", CRCL))
  )

ggplot(fig3, aes(factor(level, levels = unique(level)), Cc, fill = flcz)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(3, 8), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_grid(sex ~ panel, scales = "free_x") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 20)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Trough concentration (ng/mL)", fill = NULL,
    title = "Replicates Figure 3 of Itohara 2022"
  )
```

The typical-value troughs (no IIV, no residual error) behind the medians:

```{r fig3-typical}
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  fig3_events |> filter(rep == 1),
  keep = c("panel"), maxsteps = 500000L, returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  filter(time == 12) |>
  transmute(
    panel, WT, eGFR = CRCL,
    sex = ifelse(SEXF == 1, "Female", "Male"),
    fluconazole = CONMED_FLUCONAZOLE, trough = signif(Cc, 3)
  )
knitr::kable(typ)
```

The paper states that the median trough exceeded the 8 ng/mL upper target for
light men and fell below the 3 ng/mL lower target for heavy women not taking
fluconazole, with the rest almost within range (Results 'Monte Carlo
simulation'). The packaged model reproduces the direction of both extremes; the
assertions below check them on the typical values, which are deterministic.

```{r fig3-check}
typ_val <- function(p, w, g, s, f) {
  typ$trough[typ$panel == p & typ$WT == w & typ$eGFR == g & typ$sex == s &
    typ$fluconazole == f]
}
light_male <- typ_val("Body weight", 30, 55.2, "Male", 0)
heavy_female <- typ_val("Body weight", 90, 55.2, "Female", 0)
c(light_male = light_male, heavy_female = heavy_female)
stopifnot(
  light_male > 8,
  # The heavy-woman typical trough sits right on the 3 ng/mL boundary
  # (about 3.0 ng/mL), so the check is against a small band, not "< 3".
  heavy_female < 3.3,
  heavy_female < min(typ$trough[typ$sex == "Male"])
)
```

## Prior tacrolimus D/C ratio and everolimus CL/F (Figure 4)

Figure 4 related the post-hoc everolimus CL/F to the tacrolimus D/C ratio
(R^2 = 0.330). The prior-tacrolimus model turns that into a covariate: typical
CL/F for a 57-kg man on 1 mg/day with eGFR 55.2 and no fluconazole:

```{r fig4}
mod_tac <- readModelDb("Itohara_2022_everolimus_prior_tacrolimus")
dc <- tibble(TAC_DOSE_TROUGH_RATIO_BL = sort(c(0.44, seq(0.1, 1.5, by = 0.05)))) |>
  mutate(
    id = row_number(), time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central",
    WT = 57, DOSE_EVEROLIMUS_MGD = 1, CRCL = 55.2, SEXF = 0L, CONMED_FLUCONAZOLE = 0L
  ) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, everything())
dc_cl <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_tac), dc, returnType = "data.frame")

ggplot(dc_cl, aes(TAC_DOSE_TROUGH_RATIO_BL, cl)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 6.89, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Tacrolimus D/C ratio before everolimus (mg/(ng/mL))",
    y = "Typical everolimus CL/F (L/h)",
    caption = "Dashed line: typical CL/F of the final model without the D/C ratio (6.89 L/h)."
  )

# At the reference D/C ratio the two models give nearly the same typical CL/F.
cl_ref <- dc_cl$cl[abs(dc_cl$TAC_DOSE_TROUGH_RATIO_BL - 0.44) < 1e-9]
stopifnot(length(cl_ref) == 1, abs(cl_ref / 6.89 - 1) < 0.05)
```

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state NCA over one 12-h dosing interval of 0.5 mg twice daily for the
virtual cohort, grouped by sex and fluconazole use. The paper reports no NCA
values, so the check is internal: PKNCA's AUC over the interval must match
dose / CL for each simulated subject.

```{r pknca}
treat <- cohort |>
  transmute(id, treatment = paste(ifelse(SEXF == 1, "Female", "Male"),
    ifelse(CONMED_FLUCONAZOLE == 1, "FLCZ +", "FLCZ -"),
    sep = ", "
  ))

ss_events <- bind_rows(
  tibble(id = cohort$id, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 0.5, cmt = "depot", ii = 12, ss = 1L),
  tidyr::crossing(id = cohort$id, time = seq(0, 12, by = 0.25)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", ii = 0, ss = 0L)
) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, ii, ss, everything())

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2024)
sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ss_events, maxsteps = 500000L, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_ss$Cc), n_distinct(sim_ss$id) == n_sub)

conc <- sim_ss |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  left_join(treat, by = "id") |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose <- tibble(id = cohort$id, time = 0, amt = 0.5) |>
  left_join(treat, by = "id")

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 12,
  cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca)
```

```{r pknca-check}
cl_by_id <- sim_ss |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(cl = first(cl), .groups = "drop")
auc_chk <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  mutate(id = as.integer(id)) |>
  left_join(cl_by_id, by = "id") |>
  # dose 0.5 mg / CL (L/h) = mg*h/L; x 1000 for ng*h/mL
  mutate(expected = 1000 * 0.5 / cl, pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / expected - 1))
summary(auc_chk$pct_diff)
# Both sides use the same drawn parameters, so the only gap is the trapezoidal
# error of a 0.25-h grid over the ka = 6.07 /h absorption peak.
stopifnot(
  nrow(auc_chk) == n_sub,
  all(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff) < 3)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate distributions.** The virtual cohort draws body weight and eGFR
  from log-normal distributions centred on the Table 1 medians and truncated to
  the Table 1 ranges; the paper reports only medians and ranges.
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports IIV as CV%; it is converted with
  omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1) (0.271 -> 0.07085; 0.234 -> 0.05325).
* **Residual error.** The combined error model is encoded as
  `add(addSd) + prop(propSd)` with the Table 2 values, the proportional term
  reported as a CV and the additive as an SD in ng/mL.
* **Absorption.** `ka` is the literature value the authors held constant; the
  data had no samples within 10 h of a dose, so neither the model nor this
  vignette constrains the absorption phase.
* **Prior-tacrolimus model.** The paper prints the CL/F and Vd/F equations and
  the IIV and residual values, but no standard errors. `ka` and the allometric
  exponents are taken as held at the same values as in the final model. The
  tacrolimus D/C ratio is in mg/(ng/mL); the paper does not say whether its
  dose is the total daily dose, but the reported mean of 0.49 is consistent
  with a daily dose over a trough. The normalising value 0.44 is the one
  printed in the equation.
* **Paediatric extrapolation.** The authors applied the adult model to 13
  children (MPE -1.96 ng/mL overall, -0.706 without one infant outlier,
  Figure 5). No paediatric parameters were estimated, and the patient-level
  data needed to reproduce the MPE are not published, so it is not repeated
  here.
* **Figure 3.** The paper's 5000 replicates per scenario are reduced to 200.
  The paper describes the heavy-woman, no-fluconazole median as below the
  3 ng/mL target; the typical value from the packaged model sits at about
  3.0 ng/mL, on the boundary.
